newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Isuta can't explain drop in stock.
newsitem.headline: Isuta can't explain drop in stock.

text.p: Isuta Bhd, a maker of environment-related products, cannot account for a sharp drop in its stock price on Tuesday, its managing director said.
Chan Beng Teik, managing director of Isuta, told Reuters: "There's nothing wrong," when asked if there was a development at the company to explain the share price decline.
Isuta stock dropped 2.50 ringgit to 14.20 at 0327 GMT, and sank to as low as 13.40 earlier in the session. It was the day's most-active stock so far.

Shares of the company were suspended on Monday following a sharp rise in recent sessions and Isuta issued a statement saying that it was not aware of any rumours "or other conditions" to account for the unusual market action.

It also said in the statement sent on Monday in reply to a Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE) query that there has not been any "material development" in its business and affairs that has not been previously disclosed to the public.
Dealers said the stock could be down as syndicates cashed out after driving the price higher on talk of a possible takeover.
"After the (KLSE) query, syndicates took the chance to ramp it back down," said an institutional dealer, noting that the share price had jumped about six ringgit over the past several sessions.
Last month, businessman Soh Chee Wen was rumoured to be interested in buying a 32 percent stake in Isuta for 10.50 ringgit a share, but no announcement has since been made to confirm such a plan.
Isuta's services include the design, management and servicing of cleanrooms as well as making products such as swabs, gloves, finger cots and facemasks.
